# Tail of the length composition

## Tail cut

`tail_cut = L` excludes bins with lower bound $\geq L$ from the likelihood;
observed and predicted compositions are truncated and the predictions
renormalised,
$$
\pi_{l \mid L < L_{cut}} = \pi_l \Big/ \sum_{l' : L_{l'} < L_{cut}} \pi_{l'} .
$$
This is exact conditioning: the model still describes the whole population with
its input CVL, SPR and reference points use all lengths, and CVL needs no
adjustment. `tail_cut` is an **absolute length** (as `Lplus`), so all sensitivity
runs and ensemble draws use the same bins. (Values <= 1.5 are read as a fraction
of Linf, with a warning.)

```{r tailcut, fig.height = 4}
fit_cut <- fiticc(lfd, stklen, sel_fun = sel_fun, catch_by_gear = cbg,
                  settings = list(CVL = 0.1, obs_model = "dm", dm_theta = "saturating", tail_cut = 47))  # ~0.85 x Linf
fit_cut$tmb_data$LLB[fit_cut$tmb_data$cut_bin + 1]
plot_spr(list(no_cut = fit, cut_47 = fit_cut), ci = TRUE)
```

*Simulation* (stable F, correct Linf unless stated):

| | no cut | cut at 0.80-0.85 x Linf |
|---|---|---|
| CVL input 0.07 / 0.10 / 0.13 (true 0.1) | +9 / -1 / -11% | +13 / +9 / +4% |
| strong dome on one gear fitted as logistic | -17% | +1% |
| SPR trend recovered in a rebuild (sigmaF 0.3) | 27% | ~50% |
| Linf input 0.9 / 1.1 x true | +91 / -40% | +74 / -28% |

The cut halves the CVL sensitivity, removes the bias of a strong unmodelled dome
and roughly doubles responsiveness; it costs a small positive bias (+7 to +10%)
and more noise under stable F, and does not remove the Linf sensitivity.
Starting value: 0.80-0.85 x Linf, fixed across fits.

## Plus group, robust likelihood, GTG range

- `Lplus = L` pools bins with lower bound $\geq L$ into one (the total counts, the
  shape does not).
- `rob_eps = 0.001` bounds the cost of a few fish in bins the model barely reaches.
- The largest growth group stops at $L_\infty(1 + \text{maxsd}\cdot\text{CVL})$
  (1.3 Linf with the default `maxsd = 3` and CVL = 0.1). Fish beyond it get
  near-zero probability, and `fiticc()` warns about them (`tail_warning`,
  default `TRUE`); a tail cut makes this irrelevant.
